Graduate school included both an independent thesis and research completed through assistantships, seminars, and collaborative projects. This page separates those two strands while showing how coursework, research design, technical work, and publication contributed to my development as a geographer and GIS professional.

## Thesis Research

The thesis research began as a broad interest in volunteered geographic information, data quality, and disaster response. It developed across several graduate courses before becoming a focused study of attribute uncertainty in the Ushahidi Haiti deployment.

::: {#thesis-research}
:::

## Research Assistant Projects

My graduate research assistantships provided opportunities to contribute to applied GIScience projects while developing skills in data preparation, spatial analysis, scripting, documentation, and collaborative research.

These projects will be added as I recover and review the original materials. Planned additions include work related to predictive crime mapping and other research completed through the University of New Mexico's Earth Data Analysis Center.
